QUOTE: By default each field is really named `private_state`, `private_flags`, and so on. Code that writes `ssl->state` against the public header fails to compile, so the field is effectively private.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says opacity is enforced at compile time by renaming members to `private_*`, so the fields stay in the struct and only the name breaks. It never says the layout is hidden.
